MGR is....ok personal opinion here: MGR is awesome and terrible at the same time. It's a game of really big highs and really big lows. The parts that are frustrating and badly made are truly awful (the camera whilst indoors), and the parts that are great are some of the most fun you'll have playing a video game.

We're hoping to get one without the other. That said, we're inspired by a lot of places. Some aren't very obvious right now because only a very small fraction of the game is available/visible. The movement system is VERY important to WSW, for instance, but in D7 you really can't see everything it's got to offer.

Our custom combo system definitely takes something from God Hand, but we've tried to expand on it.

All in all though I'd say that while we do have many inspirations and we're big fans of the genre, we think WSW feels pretty unique. We hope it's in a good way.

Every good game is inspired by others, just as all good works of art build and expand on what has come before, no matter how unconventional and unique it might seem. It is much better, imo, to be honest about it, especially with oneself. The great thing that videogames have over books and films is that it is often much easier to determine what worked and what didn't, and how to change that.

I never made it far enough in MGR to get to the indoor sections, I only beat the first level the first time I played and when I returned to it the game glitched out so hard I got worried and uninstalled it. Regardless, though, I can easily imagine the camera being terrible, and I think that focusing on avoiding a similar pitfall is a sign that your team is on the right track. I am also glad to hear that you are putting so much effort into the movement system; I think that is something that too many developers take for granted and they forget that, of all the many aspects of any particular game, moving is almost always what will dominate the players' time. Making movement FUN can be the difference between a bad game and a fun game; for instance, Just Cause 2 has a terrible story and the missions are awful, but movement alone was so enjoyable (and the gameplay surrounding the movement mechanisms sufficiently solid) that people liked it. I spent over 10 hrs playing that game and never got past the third story mission.

Also, way bonus points for being inspired by God Hand, that game did not deserve to be as obscure as it is.

You and your team have opted to make a game in one of the absolute most difficult-to-develop-for genres possible (third person action combat); I can not even think of something more difficult. Gendered oppression is the systemic manner in which certain groups are privileged or disadvantaged because of their gender. Because gender is such an integral part of society, we may unconsciously subscribe to harmful and inaccurate gender stereotypes. The maintenance of gendered oppression is systemic and structural. In other words, it results from everyday practices and unquestioned assumptions within society, not necessarily from a few individuals in power. The dissemination of gendered oppression can often be subtle. Popular jokes or comments can be very effective means of spreading and maintaining harmful gendered attitudes.

Gendered oppression does not act in isolation. It intersects with discrimination based on race, sexuality, ability, class, age, history of incarceration, religion, language, and citizenship status. Analysis of any one of these oppressions alone is insufficient; each reinforces the other. The intersection of oppressions is not simply a linear combination of the individual oppressions. For example, a Black lesbian’s experience is not just the composite of a Black man’s and a white lesbian’s oppressions. The proper tackling of gendered oppression necessarily involves exploring all other forms of oppression simultaneously.
